That is the central finding of a retrospective laboratory-based surveillance study published in New Microbes and New Infections, which screened samples from MPXV-negative suspected mpox cases using two commercial multiplex PCR panels across eight health districts. The study was conducted between June 16 and August 27, 2025, as part of the national epidemic response. Two mobile laboratories, deployed at the regional hospital in Port Loko and at the Koinadugu District Government Hospital, processed clinical specimens — predominantly lesion swabs, along with a small number of vaginal swabs and crust samples — from patients meeting the World Health Organization mpox case definition. During active case searching, the definition was broadened to include anyone presenting with a severe rash, even if other criteria were not met. In total, 407 suspected mpox cases were sampled and tested for MPXV by quantitative PCR during the study window. Of these, 144 were positive, corresponding to a positivity rate of 35.7 percent, and were excluded from the differential analysis. The remaining 263 MPXV-negative samples — 252 lesion swabs, seven vaginal swabs, and four crust samples — all passed an endogenous control quality check and were retained for further testing. The researchers used the Allplex Meningitis-V1 Assay, previously validated on cutaneous samples with next-generation sequencing, to detect seven herpesviruses: herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2, varicella-zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and human herpesviruses 6 and 7. A second panel, the Allplex Genital Ulcer Assay, targeted the bacteria Haemophilus ducreyi, Treponema pallidum, and Chlamydia trachomatis, the causative agent of lymphogranuloma venereum, alongside overlapping viral targets. A sample was considered positive if a target was detected with a cycle threshold value below 35, and weak or late amplification signals were re-tested in duplicate. For the four targets covered by both panels, duplicate testing yielded 100 percent concordance. The results showed that at least one target was identified in 153 of the 263 samples, an overall detection rate of 58.2 percent. Varicella-zoster virus was by far the most frequently detected pathogen, found in 43.3 percent of patients (114 of 263; 95 percent confidence interval 37.3 to 49.6). Among the other herpesviruses, HSV-2 showed the highest detection frequency at 7.2 percent, followed by cytomegalovirus at 6.85 percent and Epstein-Barr virus at 6.1 percent. Lower rates were recorded for HHV-7 (4.6 percent), HSV-1 (1.9 percent), and HHV-6 (0.4 percent). Among bacterial targets, Haemophilus ducreyi was detected in 1.1 percent of cases, while every sample tested negative for Treponema pallidum and Chlamydia trachomatis. The study population was young: ages ranged from 1 to 80 years with a median of 18 years, and 44.5 percent of participants were aged 15 or younger. Gender information was available for 259 participants, of whom 58.7 percent were male. Statistically significant associations with age emerged for Epstein-Barr virus and HSV-2, both detected at higher proportions in older age groups, with detection rising progressively across the three age strata. Cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr virus were the only pathogens showing significant sex-based differences, both more frequent among females. Varicella-zoster virus showed no significant demographic associations, although nearly 48 percent of children aged 15 or younger tested positive compared with 39 percent of patients over 30, a difference that did not reach statistical significance. Co-detections were common and often complex. Combinations involving varicella-zoster virus were the most frequent, occurring in 19 samples, most often alongside HSV-2 and cytomegalovirus. One sample was positive for five herpesviruses simultaneously — varicella-zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, HSV-2, HHV-7, and Epstein-Barr virus — and two samples carried triple viral infections. Haemophilus ducreyi was exclusively co-detected with varicella-zoster virus, on two occasions, a molecular co-detection the authors describe as rarely reported. Among co-detections not involving varicella-zoster virus, nine of ten included Epstein-Barr virus. The authors caution that, given the small numbers, no inference about biological interaction between co-detected pathogens can be made. Geographically, the highest sample numbers came from Port Loko and Tonkolili, and detections of at least one target exceeded undiagnosed cases in five of the eight surveyed districts. Varicella-zoster virus was the only pathogen identified in every district where positive cases were found, with the largest counts in Koinadugu, Falaba, and Port Loko. The distribution of other pathogens varied: HSV-2 and cytomegalovirus clustered in Port Loko and Tonkolili, Epstein-Barr virus in Kambia, and HHV-7 in Kambia and Bombali. One observation carries particular public health weight. The retrospective screening identified Haemophilus ducreyi in three samples collected months before an outbreak of Haemophilus ducreyi-associated skin ulceration was officially declared in Sierra Leone for the first time in December 2025, with the reported likely index case showing symptom onset on October 1, 2025. The authors stress that their findings do not establish an epidemiological link between these three patients and the subsequent outbreak, but they argue that real-time differential testing could potentially have provided an early warning signal prompting further investigation. The study has notable limitations. Samples and epidemiological data were originally collected for the mpox response, leaving critical clinical information — including symptoms, HIV status, and patient outcomes — incomplete, so the clinical impact of co-detections could not be assessed. MPXV-positive samples were not included in the differential testing, sequencing was not performed, and the study period covered neither the entire outbreak timeline nor every district in Sierra Leone. The authors also note that pathogen distributions can vary seasonally, meaning the findings represent a temporal snapshot rather than a complete annual profile, which may partly explain the absence of Chlamydia trachomatis and Treponema pallidum detections. Even so, the results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating multiplex molecular screening into outbreak response, particularly when combined with mobile laboratory deployment, to reduce diagnostic dead ends and uncover pathogens circulating beneath the epidemiological signal of a dominant outbreak agent. In the same two months of 2025 the city counted only 10, so this year’s figure is more than seven times higher. Brazil as a whole has 665 cases so far in 2026, according to the minister. PHOTO: FILE KARACHI: Sindh has reported another case of mpox, prompting the Health Department to convene a meeting to review surveillance, early diagnosis and measures to contain the spread of the virus. A woman who tested positive for mpox has been shifted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital at Nipa. According to hospital officials, she was brought to the facility two days ago, where samples were collected for a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test. The infection was confirmed after the test results became available. Hospital officials said seven mpox patients were currently receiving treatment at the facility. According to figures available with the Health Department, Sindh has reported 98 mpox cases and 12 deaths so far this year. However, sources said the latest case had taken the cumulative number of infections reported during the year beyond 100. Against this backdrop, a meeting of Health Department officials was convened under the chairmanship of the director general Health Services Sindh to review the situation and assess measures to prevent further transmission. Attendees at the meeting included the director Health Services Karachi Division, a professor of pathology at Dow University and director of the Provincial Public Health Laboratory Sindh, Professor Dr Saeed Khan. The chief executive officer of the Sindh Healthcare Commission was also invited, while Additional Director of the Provincial Disease Surveillance and Response Unit (PDSRU) Sindh, Dr Asif Syed. Participants reviewed arrangements for monitoring cases, identifying suspected patients at an early stage and ensuring timely reporting of infections. Discussions also focused on laboratory testing of suspected cases, identifying people who had come into contact with infected individuals and ensuring their continued monitoring. Officials further examined measures to strengthen infection prevention and control at public and private hospitals and healthcare centres, improve early diagnosis and ensure that confirmed and suspected cases were promptly reported to the relevant authorities. records.content: Dangerous Mpox Strain Found Abroad May Be Spreading in Central California A more dangerous strain of mpox may be spreading within California's Stanislaus County. Health officials announced four reported cases, with two confirmed as clade I and two awaiting results. Three of the four people had not traveled outside the country. Clade I is typically associated with international travel and can cause more serious illness than clade II, especially among immunocompromised people. Its mortality rate ranges between 1 percent and 10 percent. Officials say the risk to the general public remains low. Mpox usually spreads through close skin-to-skin contact. It can cause fever, muscle weakness and painful sores resembling pimples or blisters. Symptoms can begin 21 days after exposure and last between two and four weeks. People diagnosed should isolate until their rash disappears. Health officials recommend recognizing symptoms, getting vaccinated if at risk of exposure and seeking medical care when needed. Most people recover on their own, but severe cases can be treated with antivirals. Vaccination appointments are available through the Stanislaus County Immunization Clinic

REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo comments Join our Whatsapp Channel KARACHI: Another child tested positive for mpox in the city on Friday, raising the tally of the viral infectious disease this year so far in the province to 115. Mpox is a viral infection which was earlier restricted to international travellers. It spreads through close contact with someone who has mpox, contaminated bedding, towels, medical instruments, surfaces or objects. Sources said the three-year-old boy was currently under treatment at Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre (SIDH&RC). “Like the recent two cases, this child also underwent circumcision at the same Malir hospital that has been officially sealed over concerns related to lack of infection control measures,” a hospital doctor said, adding that an infant with mpox died early this week after remaining under treatment for 10 days at the facility while another was in the intensive care. He also shared that the seven mpox patients currently under treatment at SIDH&RC included the mother and an aunt of the infant who died fighting mpox — the first infant’s death in Karachi this year. With the latest case, the total number of mpox cases reported this year so far at SIDH&RC has risen to 31, while in the province to 115 with 12 deaths. The Sindh Health Care Commission (SHCC) had sealed Ibne Hassan Hospital over 10 days ago following a laboratory report confirming an mpox case in an infant, after concerns were identified regarding infection prevention and control practices. “The hospital was legal but not registered with the SHCC. The team sealed the facility following reports that a child seemed to have contracted mpox there. The team during inspection found a dispenser conducting circumcision, a procedure that was beyond his scope,” explained Dr Ahson Qavi Siddiqi, the chief executive officer of SHCC. The hospital, he said, was opened on Friday for sanitisation, fumigation and disinfection, and sealed again. “This exercise will continue for some time and then sampling [to see if the facility is safe and fit for operation] will be carried out. records.content: TODAY’S PAPER | November 02, 2026 | EPAPER ☰ Home Latest Pakistan Business World Sports Opinion Life & Style T-Magazine Blogs Tech Cartoon Home Khyber Pakhtunkhwa K-P reports four new mpox cases Health authorities step up contact tracing as tally tops 18 Shahida Parveen October 28, 2026 1 min read facebook twitter whatsup linkded email K-P reported first locally transmitted MPOX case. PHOTO: FILE PESHAWAR: Four new mpox cases have been reported in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, taking the provincial tally for the year to 18 and prompting health authorities to trace the patients' contacts amid concerns about ocal transmission. None of the patients, including one woman and three men, has a reported history of international travel, the health department said. Samples sent to the Public Health Reference Laboratory at Khyber Medical University confirmed the infections. Two patients are from Nowshera, one from Peshawar and one from Mardan. All four have been advised to isolate at home to prevent further spread. One patient has died and 13 have recovered from mpox in the province this year, according to the health department. The first case was reported on January 9. People with mpox are infectious and can pass the disease on to others until all sores have healed and a new layer of skin has formed. Children, pregnant people and people with weak immune systems are at risk for complications from mpox. Typically for mpox, fever, muscle aches and sore throat appear first. The mpox rash begins on the face and spreads over the body, extending to the palms of the hands and soles of the feet and evolves over 2-4 weeks in stages – macules, papules, vesicles, pustules. Lesions dip in the centre before crusting over. Scabs then fall off. Lymphadenopathy (swollen lymph nodes) is a classic feature of mpox. Some people can be infected without developing any symptoms. In the context of the global outbreak of mpox which began in 2022 (caused mostly by Clade IIb virus), the illness begins differently in some people. In just over a half of cases, a rash may appear before or at the same time as other symptoms and does not always progress over the body. The first lesion can be in the groin, anus, or in or around the mouth. People with mpox can become very sick. Onstage in Pasadena This Week Virtual Guide to Pasadena Area Schools Guide to Summer Camps Community News Pasadena City Manager Proclaims Monkeypox a Local Emergency Published on Thursday, August 18, 2022 | 4:35 pm Monkeypox Virus courtesy of PPHD Interim City Manager Cynthia Kurtz has proclaimed a local emergency to strengthen the City’s preparedness and ability to respond to the virus. In an effort to stop the spread of monkeypox and make the monkeypox vaccine more readily accessible to those at highest risk, Pasadena Public Health Department (PPHD) is also expanding the eligibility criteria for the vaccine, effective immediately. “We are continuing to work proactively to protect the health of our community, and this proclamation allows us to mobilize more resources,” Kurtz said. “This local emergency will allow us to continue to support our community members who are currently most at-risk, while also to better prepare for what’s to come.” Currently, PPHD has 15 confirmed or probable cases of monkeypox in Pasadena. There are reportedly 2,356 cases in California as of Aug. 17, according to the California Department of Public Health. The proclamation allows the City to take all actions necessary to implement preventive measures to protect and preserve public health, including, but not limited to, mobilizing City resources, accelerating emergency planning; streamlining staffing; coordinating across other agencies; expediting the ability of the City to purchase necessary supplies to combat monkeypox; allowing for future reimbursement by the state and federal governments; and raising awareness throughout Pasadena about monkeypox, including how people can lower their risk and stop the spread. Earlier this month, Governor Gavin Newsom proclaimed a state of emergency to support the state’s response to monkeypox. Additionally, Los Angeles and Orange Counties have issued similar proclamations to bolster their preparedness. PPHD continues to provide monkeypox vaccines by invitation only to the following select groups of persons identified through public health investigation: • Gay or bisexual men and transgender persons who had multiple or anonymous sex partners in the last 14 days, including engaging in survival and/or transactional sex (e.g., sex in exchange for shelter, food and other goods and needs).Persons confirmed to have had high- or intermediate-risk contact with someone with monkeypox, as defined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). • Persons who attended an event/venue where there was high risk of exposure to an individual(s) with confirmed monkeypox virus through skin-to-skin or sexual contact. Public health officials will work with event/venue organizers to identify persons who may have been present and at risk of exposure while at the venue. • Persons experiencing homelessness (PEH) with high-risk behaviors. • People in high-risk cohorts identified by clinical staff in the LA County Jail system. • Gay or bisexual men and transgender persons who: – Were diagnosed with gonorrhea or early syphilis within the past 12 months; or – Are on HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP); or – Attended or worked at a commercial sex venue or other venue where they had anonymous sex or sex with multiple partners (e.g., saunas, bathhouses, sex clubs, sex parties) within past 21 days. Vaccine eligibility and information on how to access vaccines will continue to be updated at www.cityofpasadena.net/monkeypox. Monkeypox is a viral infection that can spread through contact with body fluids, monkeypox sores, or shared items (such as clothing and bedding) that have been contaminated with fluids from sores of a person with monkeypox. Although monkeypox is not generally considered a sexually transmitted infection, it can be transmitted during sex through prolonged skin-to-skin and other intimate contact, regardless of gender or sexual orientation. To prevent the spread of monkeypox, PPHD recommends: • Avoiding close physical contact with people who have symptoms, including sores or rashes; • Talking to your sexual partner(s) about any recent illness and being aware of new or unexplained sores or rashes; • Avoiding contact with contaminated materials; • Wearing personal protective equipment (i.e., mask, gloves, gown) if you cannot avoid close contact with someone who has symptoms; • Practicing good hand hygiene; • Speaking to your healthcare provider about getting tested if you have symptoms; and • Staying in isolation until you are no longer considered infectious per public health guidance. For questions regarding monkeypox, public health officials recommend that you speak to your primary care provider. If you do not have a regular provider, call LA County 211 for assistance. In addition, people without a regular provider that have developed a rash in the genital or perianal area, can access services at Los Angeles County’s sexual health clinics. The Stanislaus County Health Services Agency said four cases of Clade 1 mpox were recently reported to them, with two of them confirmed by the California Department of Public Health. Advertisement There is additionally testing underway to possibly confirm the other two cases, health officials said. Stanislaus County HSA said three of the people tested reported no recent international travel and the travel history of the fourth person is still being investigated. Clade 1 mpox cases in the U.S. were commonly linked to international travel, but Stanislaus County HSA said since August, more cases have been reported among people without recent trips outside of the country. Still, health officials said the risk to the public remains low and there is no evidence that suggests mpox is spreading across California or the U.S. "While we have identified four cases in our county, we want residents to know that the risk to the general public remains low," said Stanislaus County Public Health Officer Dr. Thea Pasasozomentos. "Being aware of the symptoms, getting vaccinated if at risk of exposure to mpox, and seeking medical care when needed are important ways to protect yourself and prevent the spread of mpox. Mpox can be spread through close contact like touching or sex or contaminated materials like sheets, clothing and needles. Initial symptoms include fever, chills, exhaustion, and muscle weakness, followed by a painful or itchy rash with raised lesions that scab over. records.content: News Health Three-year-old boy diagnosed with mpox in Karachi — Dawn UA.NEWS 31 October 2026 09:02 A three-year-old boy in Karachi, Pakistan, has been confirmed to have mpox. This brought the number of infection cases registered in Sindh province since the beginning of the year to 115, Dawn reports . Treatment of the child According to the publication's sources, the boy is being treated at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre. A doctor at the facility said that the child, like two recent patients, underwent circumcision at a hospital in Malir district, which was sealed over concerns about compliance with infection-control measures. According to the doctor, an infant with mpox died at the centre early this week after 10 days of treatment. Another patient was in the intensive care unit. Among the seven patients currently being treated at the centre are the mother and aunt of the deceased infant. Hospital inspection Including the new patient, the centre in Karachi has recorded 31 mpox cases since the beginning of the year. Sindh province has registered 115 infection cases and 12 deaths. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . More than 10 days ago, the Sindh Healthcare Commission sealed Ibn Hassan Hospital after laboratory confirmation of mpox in an infant and due to identified shortcomings in infection prevention and control measures. The commission's chief executive officer, Ahsan Qavi Siddiqui, said that the medical facility was operating legally but was not registered with the commission. During the inspection, he said, officials found an employee performing circumcisions beyond the scope of their authority. The hospital was temporarily reopened for sanitisation, fumigation and disinfection, and was then sealed again. Once this work is completed, samples are planned to be taken there to determine whether the facility is safe and fit to operate. Read us on Download our app

The finding, drawn from 155 doctors working in family medicine and pediatric outpatient settings across all seven states of the zone, points to a substantial gap in the preparedness of the clinicians most likely to encounter the first suspicious cases of a re-emerging zoonotic disease. The study set out to quantify how well this frontline workforce in northwestern Nigeria understands the disease, and to identify which sociodemographic and professional characteristics are associated with better knowledge. The participants were an experienced group. Their mean age was 38.8 years with a standard deviation of 7.4, and 60.7% were men. Most respondents, 77.4%, worked in general outpatient clinics, 63.2% had accumulated at least ten years of practice experience, and 36.1% were senior registrars. Despite this seniority profile, only 18.9% reported any prior experience diagnosing or managing a Mpox case, a detail that helps contextualize the knowledge results that followed. When knowledge was scored, the results were strikingly low. Just nine of the 155 participants, or 5.8%, achieved the threshold the investigators defined as good knowledge of Mpox. Discover more Track Outbreaks Book Care Services Check Symptoms Read Med Journals The mean overall knowledge score across the cohort was 61.7%, with a standard deviation of 12.5 percentage points, indicating that the typical physician answered roughly three-fifths of the knowledge items correctly. The authors conclude that this represents a significant gap in participants’ understanding of the various aspects of the disease. The inferential analysis identified three factors associated with higher mean knowledge scores. Physicians with ten or more years of practice experience scored significantly higher than their less experienced colleagues, with a p-value of 0.049. Senior professional cadres also performed better, an association that reached statistical significance at p = 0.031. Most notably, doctors who had been involved in diagnosing or managing Mpox at some point in their careers showed higher knowledge scores, with p = 0.021. Even so, the authors emphasize that these higher scores remained suboptimal, meaning that experience and seniority improved knowledge only partially and did not bring most clinicians to a good-knowledge standard. The cross-sectional design imposes important limits on how these findings can be interpreted. Because data were collected at a single point in time through an online survey, the study can describe associations but cannot establish causal relationships between professional characteristics and knowledge. The nationwide cross-sectional survey interviewed 5,177 participants aged 15 years and older across five provinces of Burundi between March and December 2025. The survey used a structured questionnaire adapted from the Africa CDC behavioural and social sciences framework for mpox. Overall, 94.7 percent of participants had heard about mpox. Recognition of symptoms was strong: 94.4 percent correctly identified skin rash and 84.3 percent identified fever as common symptoms, and 86.6 percent recognized direct contact as a mode of transmission. Knowledge of the causative agent was markedly weaker. Some 21.4 percent of participants incorrectly identified bacteria as the cause of mpox, which is caused by a virus, and 24.5 percent did not know the causative agent at all. Taken together, nearly half of those surveyed held an incorrect view or no view on what causes the disease. Discover more Check Symptoms Read Med Journals Buy Maps Shop African Art Radio emerged as the dominant channel for health information, cited as the main source of mpox information by 82.0 percent of participants and as the most trusted source by 87.0 percent. The researchers analysed factors associated with knowledge and with prevention and control practices using bivariate and multivariable analyses, applying modified Poisson regression models with generalized estimating equations. Higher income was associated with better mpox knowledge, while prevention and control practices varied by knowledge level, income, marital status, and HIV status. Vaccine awareness was low despite apparent readiness to accept immunization. Although 86.1 percent of participants were unaware that an mpox vaccine is available, 76.5 percent reported willingness to accept vaccination if it were offered to them. The survey’s context matters. Mpox remains an important public health concern in Africa, particularly following the spread of clade Ib in several countries, and limited information had previously been available on Burundian population knowledge, risk perception, preventive behaviours, and willingness to accept mpox vaccination. The study was designed to assess social and behavioural factors associated with mpox preparedness among the general population. The authors caution that sampling weights were not applied, so the findings should be interpreted as estimates among surveyed participants rather than nationally weighted population estimates. Univariate analyses were used to describe key variables, and the cross-sectional design captures a snapshot rather than changes over time. The overall picture is one of high awareness paired with incomplete understanding. Most people surveyed knew the disease, its main symptoms, and its principal route of transmission, yet misconceptions about the causative agent were widespread, and knowledge was unevenly distributed across income groups. Discover more Explore History Find Vaccines vaccine The researchers conclude that, despite high awareness and willingness to accept vaccination, important gaps in mpox knowledge remain, particularly among lower-income groups, and that strengthening accessible and targeted risk communication strategies will be essential to improve mpox preparedness in Burundi. Bavarian Nordic to Supply and Donate Vaccines for Global Mpox Emergency Stockpile Bavarian Nordic A/S Tue, October 27, 2026 at 8:52 AM PDT 4 min read BAVA.CO -0.97% Bavarian Nordic A/S Bavarian Nordic donates 75,000 doses of MVA-BN® and will also supply 150,000 doses to new global mpox vaccine emergency stockpile. Building emergency reserves is an important milestone in global mpox preparedness, helping ensure timely and equitable access to vaccines. This new initiative reflects Bavarian Nordic's longstanding role as a trusted partner in global health security and its mission to protect people and communities, and save lives, through vaccines. COPENHAGEN, Denmark, October 27, 2026 – Bavarian Nordic A/S (OMX: BAVA) today announced that it will strengthen global preparedness for mpox through a donation of 75,000 doses of its MVA-BN® vaccine to the newly established global mpox vaccine emergency stockpile, helping ensure that protection is available when and where it is needed. The creation of a new stockpile marks an important milestone in global mpox preparedness, helping to ensure timely and equitable access to vaccines and enabling effective outbreak response for communities around the world. It is managed by the International Coordinating Group (ICG) on Vaccine Provision, a mechanism hosted by WHO that coordinates the allocation and deployment of emergency vaccine supplies to countries responding to outbreaks. Initial funding for the stockpile has been provided by Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance. The donation complements a newly awarded contract to supply 150,000 doses to the stockpile. Bavarian Nordic's contribution through both vaccine supply and donation reflects its longstanding commitment to global health security and its mission to protect people and communities, and save lives, through vaccines. Hitesh Sahni, Senior Vice President, Public Preparedness at Bavarian Nordic, said: "Infectious diseases do not stop at borders, and communities need timely access to protection when outbreaks occur. The establishment of a global mpox vaccine emergency stockpile is an important milestone in strengthening preparedness for future outbreaks. Ensuring timely and equitable access to vaccines is critical to protecting populations and enabling an effective public health response. We are proud to embark on a new collaboration with ICG partners to build a more coordinated and resilient response to the recurring threat of mpox." About the smallpox/mpox vaccine MVA-BN, or Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic, is the only non-replicating mpox vaccine approved in the U.S., Switzerland, Singapore and Mexico (marketed as JYNNEOS®), Canada (marketed as IMVAMUNE®), and the EU/EAA and United Kingdom (marketed as IMVANEX®). It was originally developed as a smallpox vaccine in collaboration with the U.S. government to ensure the supply of a smallpox vaccine for the US population, including immunocompromised individuals who are not recommended vaccination with replicating smallpox vaccines. MVA-BN is now indicated for use for individuals considered at risk for smallpox or mpox infection. Story Continues Bavarian Nordic has been a long-term supplier of the vaccine to national stockpiles. During the 2022-2024 mpox outbreaks, the Company supported governments and international organizations by expanding access to the vaccine to more than 70 countries worldwide. In 2024, MVA-BN received WHO prequalification for the use of the vaccine by individuals aged 12 years and older, enabling procurement through the UN agency focusing on children's health. More recently, the European Commission approved an extension of the vaccine's marketing authorization in the EU/EEA to include children aged 2 to under 12 years. This expanded indication further helps to address the unmet need for mpox vaccines among younger populations at increased risk of infection. Bavarian Nordic is working with global partners on additional clinical studies to further expand the availability of MVA-BN for other vulnerable populations. In parallel, the Company is developing new manufacturing processes to allow for scaling of capacity to meet increased demand in the future. The system, called ChronoGate, uses a thermosensitive poloxamer to hold the detection machinery apart from the amplification reaction in both time and space, and it was applied to detect the monkeypox virus (MPXV) using the viral F3L gene as the target. The problem the platform addresses is well known in the field of point-of-care testing. Real-time quantitative PCR remains the gold standard for pathogen detection, but it depends on professional laboratory conditions and is poorly suited to on-site use. CRISPR/Cas12a technology offers high specificity, yet its sensitivity on its own is limited, so it requires preamplification, typically by recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA). The conventional two-step RPA-CRISPR workflow, in which amplification and detection are carried out sequentially in separate handling stages, is prone to aerosol contamination. One-step systems such as SHERLOCKv2 avoid that handling but suffer from template competition, which reduces sensitivity by a reported 10- to 100-fold. ChronoGate’s solution is a temporal-spatial separation strategy built on the phase behaviour of poloxamer. At temperatures below 25 °C, the poloxamer encapsulates the Cas12a protein together with its guide CRISPR RNA (crRNA), keeping the detection components physically separated from the amplification mixture. When the reaction is heated to 37 °C, the poloxamer releases the Cas12a/crRNA complex with a delay of approximately 8 minutes, allowing RPA amplification to proceed first and detection to begin afterwards within the same closed tube. This ordered “amplification-first, detection-later” sequence preserves the sensitivity of a two-step workflow while eliminating the tube-opening steps that create aerosol contamination risk. The researchers determined the optimal reaction conditions to be 15% (w/v) poloxamer in a 15 μL reaction volume. Alongside the chemistry, the team developed a companion portable fluorescence detector to read out the Cas12a signal, making the whole system usable outside a standard laboratory. Performance was assessed using the monkeypox virus F3L gene as the detection target. The platform achieved an encapsulation efficiency of 85.7%, meaning most of the Cas12a/crRNA complex was successfully sequestered by the poloxamer during the low-temperature setup phase. Sensitivity testing with serial dilutions of plasmid DNA showed a detection limit of 1 copy/μL, which the authors report as comparable to the conventional two-step method. That result is significant because it indicates the one-step format did not pay the usual sensitivity penalty associated with template competition in mixed one-pot reactions. Specificity was evaluated by testing nontarget pathogens alongside the MPXV target. No cross-reactivity was observed, which the researchers cite as confirmation of good specificity for the assay. The platform was then applied to clinical samples. Among 14 clinical specimens tested, the ChronoGate results showed 100% concordance with qPCR, the reference method. Total detection time was only 40 minutes, which the authors describe as a 56% improvement in speed compared with qPCR. The sample size is small, and the findings come from a brief report, so the clinical validation should be read as an initial demonstration rather than a large-scale performance evaluation. The authors conclude that the ChronoGate RPA-CRISPR platform enables rapid, sensitive, and specific single-tube one-step detection with simple operation and high portability. In their framing, it provides a reliable point-of-care testing solution for monkeypox virus and potentially other pathogens in resource-limited settings, where the laboratory infrastructure required for qPCR is often unavailable. More broadly, the work illustrates how material properties can be used to choreograph molecular reactions. By exploiting the temperature-dependent gel-sol transition of poloxamer, the platform converts a timing problem—when should detection start relative to amplification—into a physical barrier that dissolves on cue. If the approach generalises to other pathogen targets, it could simplify the design of closed-tube CRISPR diagnostics that retain two-step sensitivity without two-step handling, a persistent trade-off in the development of field-deployable nucleic acid tests. The government of Western Equatoria State has unveiled plans to build a laboratory to strengthen disease surveillance and improve rapid detection of infectious threats such as Ebola and Mpox. Speaking at the site, the governor said the project reflects the government’s commitment to protecting public health. “We have come to the site that’s going to be ended over to the engineer to carry the construction of the reference laboratory of high tech and on behalf of the people of Western Equatoria and the government on my own behalf,” he said. He noted that the land has now been handed over to engineers to begin building a modern, high-tech reference laboratory on behalf of the people of Western Equatoria. Written by Siyang Pei, Saqib Ali, Shixin Ma, Aizhen Guo and Pan Tao, the review organizes poxvirus antigens not as a simple catalog of immunogenic molecules but according to virion localization, sequence conservation, antibody function and translational readiness, spanning the genera Orthopoxvirus, Capripoxvirus and Parapoxvirus. The authors frame their synthesis against a persistent disease burden. Poxviruses complicate this task with a complex virion architecture: two principal infectious forms, the intracellular mature virion and the extracellular enveloped virion, and genomes encoding roughly 130 to 220 proteins depending on the species. Mature virion antigens are typically tied to attachment, entry and neutralization, whereas enveloped virion antigens are linked to cell-to-cell spread, dissemination and antibody effector mechanisms. Using vaccinia virus as the reference framework, the review details the major mature virion surface antigens. H3, a 324-amino-acid protein of about 37.5 kilodaltons, is an immunodominant component that binds cell-surface heparan sulfate and mediates virion attachment. Its ectodomain adopts a mixed beta/alpha/beta fold with a broad positively charged surface consistent with a glycosaminoglycan-binding interface. Human H3-specific antibodies induced by vaccination have shown cross-neutralization or protection against multiple orthopoxviruses, including mpox and cowpox viruses, in experimental models. Notably, epitope mapping showed that V13I or D15N substitutions did not abolish antibody binding but converted a neutralizing epitope into a non-neutralizing one, indicating that neutralization depends on structural context rather than binding alone. Discover more Check Symptoms Read Med Journals Study Biology vaccine vaccines D8, a roughly 32-kilodalton mature virion membrane protein, promotes adsorption by binding chondroitin sulfate, particularly chondroitin sulfate E, through a carbonic anhydrase homology domain with a positively charged central dome. Antibody mapping revealed that monoclonal antibodies whose footprints overlap this dome differ markedly in their ability to block the D8-chondroitin sulfate interaction, and the neutralizing antibody LA5 prevents engagement of chondroitin sulfate by traversing the binding surface. Unlike H3, D8 appears restricted to Orthopoxvirus, lacking detectable homologs in the representative capripoxvirus and parapoxvirus genomes analyzed, which makes it especially relevant for orthopoxvirus-focused serology. A27, a small 14-kilodalton surface protein, carries a flexible N-terminal heparin-binding domain and assembles mainly as a homotrimer whose coiled-coil architecture may organize multiple binding domains to increase avidity. Antibodies mainly recognize the N-terminal region spanning amino acids 21 to 40 and a C-terminal region spanning amino acids 81 to 110, but neutralizing activity concentrates among antibodies targeting the heparin-binding region. Even among closely related homologs, limited substitutions matter: the mpox virus homolog A29 differs by only three residues in this domain, yet a mpox-specific monoclonal antibody recognizing the A29 N terminus is non-neutralizing and fails to bind other orthopoxvirus A27 homologs broadly. L1 stands apart from these attachment proteins. It is a myristoylated membrane protein that functions in a glycosaminoglycan-independent entry pathway as part of the entry-fusion complex, and its N-myristoylation is critical for producing infectious virions. L1-specific neutralizing antibodies target conformational epitopes, with residue D35 identified as a key determinant of a shared vulnerable surface recognized by antibodies 2D5 and 7D11. L1 is highly conserved across the family, and recent mapping of the mpox virus homolog M1 showed that the D35-centered surface is retained there; alanine substitution of D35 markedly reduces antibody binding to the virus. On the enveloped virion, A33 and B5 dominate. A33 is a glycosylated protein forming a butterfly-shaped disulfide-linked homodimer with a C-type lectin-like domain. Antibodies targeting the variable apical loop show restricted breadth, whereas the antibody A27D7, which recognizes the more conserved dimerization groove, binds multiple orthopoxvirus homologs and protects in a mouse model. Human anti-A35 antibodies isolated from mpox-convalescent individuals target the homologous groove, block viral spread and protect mice and macaques. B5, a type I transmembrane glycoprotein with four short consensus repeat motifs, accounts for much of the enveloped virion-neutralizing capacity of vaccinia immune globulin, and efficient neutralization generally requires complement, meaning binding titers alone do not predict protection. Discover more Vaccines Find Vaccines Track Outbreaks Manage Livestock Book Lab Tests On the vaccine side, the review concludes that single-antigen strategies are usually insufficient. H3 alone protected roughly 80 percent of mice against a low-dose intranasal vaccinia challenge but failed to protect in a multivalent mpox mRNA vaccine study, whereas the multivalent formulation achieved complete protection. A27-based protection proved highly dependent on antigen format and challenge model, and a variola virus A27 formulation induced high antibody titers but failed to protect mice. L1 performed best when conformationally intact and well-adjuvanted, with a pseudovirus nanoparticle displaying L1 providing complete survival after lethal challenge. The classical four-antigen concept combining A27 and L1 with A33 and B5 illustrates the guiding principle: complementary coverage of both infectious forms and of antibody effector mechanisms. For diagnostics, the review distinguishes exposure-level screening from differentiation of infected from vaccinated individuals. Conserved, immunodominant antigens such as H3, D8 and A27 homologs maximize sensitivity but cannot reliably distinguish mpox infection from prior vaccinia-based vaccination. The mpox homolog E8 provided the strongest separation between mpox-positive and pre-outbreak negative samples in recent multiplex evaluations. Differential strategies instead exploit antigenic differences: B22-family proteins, absent from vaccinia virus, support mpox-specific and capripoxvirus DIVA assays, while ratio-based comparisons of vaccinia B5 and mpox B6 reactivity improved discrimination between infection- and vaccination-associated responses. The authors emphasize that cross-reactive binding, direct neutralization, spread inhibition, animal protection and cross-protection must be treated as distinct evidence levels, and that conserved structural motifs should remain testable hypotheses until functional endpoints are demonstrated. The vaccinia-centered framework transfers most reliably within Orthopoxvirus, where direct evidence for neutralization and protection is concentrated; its extension to capripoxviruses and parapoxviruses requires antigen-by-antigen, epitope-level validation in natural hosts. For vaccines and antibody countermeasures, the strongest current candidates are multivalent or multi-epitope targeting of mature and enveloped virion antigens, especially L1, A33 and B5, while future work points toward single-cell B-cell profiling, deep mutational scanning and structural prediction to identify functional conformational epitopes that survive authentic-virus and in vivo testing. records.content: 整合结构分析揭示痘病毒核心内多聚体孔道复合物的分子架构 《Nature Communications》:A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月31日 来源:Nature Communications 18.1 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Article Open access 长期以来已知痘病毒(poxvirus)可在其核心(core)内转录一百多种早期信使RNA(messenger RNA, mRNA),然而这些转录本如何离开核心仍属未知。研究人员将冷冻电子断层扫描(cryo-electron tomography, cryo-ET)与基于深度学习的颗粒挑选(deep-learning-based particle picking)、亚断层图平均(subtomogram averaging, STA)、交联质谱(cross-linking mass spectrometry, XL-MS)以及AlphaFold3(AF3)建模相结合,解析了痘病毒核心内这一长期寻求的孔道(pore)的分子架构。该孔道由病毒蛋白E8、E6与L3的异源组装形成,共同构建出跨越核心壁(core wall)及表面暴露栅栏层(palisade layer)的空心六聚体管。在孔道通道内,研究人员观察到一种与病毒RNA解旋酶(viral RNA helicase) I8形态一致的杆状密度,其可能参与新合成病毒mRNA自核心的释放。研究人员进一步观察到,在转录条件下存在缺乏外环(outer ring)与基环(basal ring)的孔道状态。上述发现共同鉴定了双链DNA病毒表面层内一个候选mRNA释放孔(mRNA-release pore)的结构与动态特征,并提示该结构可能构成痘病毒转录机器(transcription machinery)的一部分。 **研究背景** 索取肿瘤靶点蛋白研究最新资料 领 取 痘病毒(poxvirus)是在宿主细胞质内复制的双链DNA病毒,涵盖天花病毒(Variola virus)与引发Mpox(猴痘)国际关注的突发公共卫生事件的Mpox病毒。其成熟病毒粒子(mature virion, MV)呈砖形,包裹双凹核心(core)及侧体(lateral bodies)。病毒进入细胞后,核心被释放至细胞质,其内转录机器可立即启动一百余种早期信使RNA(messenger RNA, mRNA)的合成,转录本随后释放入细胞质供翻译。然而,这些mRNA如何跨越核心壁(core wall)离开核心,数十年来悬而未决。早期研究虽在核心表面栅栏层(palisade layer)中观察到由A10三聚体环绕的孔状结构并推测其为mRNA释放位点,但分辨率限制使其蛋白组成无法确证,构成理解痘病毒早期基因表达的关键空白。 **研究开展、主要结论与意义** 针对这一空白,研究人员以牛痘病毒(vaccinia virus, VACV)为对象,整合冷冻电子断层扫描(cryo-electron tomography, cryo-ET)、亚断层图平均(subtomogram averaging, STA)、交联质谱(cross-linking mass spectrometry, XL-MS)与AlphaFold3(AF3)建模,首次解析痘病毒核心内多聚体孔道复合物的分子架构(分辨率约8.2 ?)。研究确定孔道由E8、E6与L3组装成跨越核心壁与栅栏层的三层空心管道,并提示管腔中央杆状密度可能对应病毒RNA解旋酶(I8),为“痘病毒核心mRNA释放孔”假说提供了首个结构性实证。该工作发表于《Nature Communications》,深化了对痘病毒早期基因表达结构基础的认识。 **主要技术方法** 研究人员将纯化的VACV Western Reserve株无膜核心与三磷酸核苷(NTP)转录缓冲液孵育5分钟后快速冷冻,采集89个倾斜序列(tilt series)行cryo-ET与STA;建立整合3D U-Net分割、GAPSTOP模板匹配与表面法向过滤的自动化颗粒挑选流程;采用二琥珀酰亚胺亚砜(DSSO)交联剂行XL-MS鉴定相互作用蛋白;利用AF3及AF3x对候选蛋白行单体至十二聚体预测并密度拟合建模;另以感染复数(MOI) 100感染HeLa细胞30分钟行原位cryo-ET验证。 **研究结果** (一)VACV核心经cryo-ET分析。转录激活的核心侧体脱离、基因组解聚,部分核心壁破裂;栅栏层保持不变,顶部视角可见六个A10三聚体环绕的孔状结构。 (二)自动化孔道颗粒挑选的高通量流程。整合3D U-Net分割、GAPSTOP模板匹配与表面几何过滤建立自动化流程,以32个人工挑选孔道平均作为初始模板,从119个核心中获得2,678个颗粒用于精细STA。 (三)孔道复合物是由六个A10三聚体支撑的六聚体管。STA获得约8.1 ?分辨率重建,显示孔道为直径约15 nm、高约20 nm的六聚体管(含周围A10三聚体时直径约30 nm),含外环、内环、基环及中央杆状密度,C 6 对称性经随机化检验确认源自数据本身。 (四)XL-MS鉴定孔道复合物组分。XL-MS在两个生物学重复中鉴定出233个蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用(protein-protein interactions, PPIs);E6与周围A10三聚体交联,L3同时与A10、E6及核心壁蛋白A3交联;结合AF3预测与密度全局搜索,确定E8六聚体占据外环、E6六聚体占据内环、L3占据基环,A3因拟合较差而归入核心壁。 (五)孔道复合物的拓扑与结构域组织。E8外环N端朝向组装中心、C端位于基部,相邻原聚体经保守极性网络连接;E6结构域1夹于E8单体对之间,结构域2以N-C端互作稳定环化;L3十二聚体中,内环衬于中央通道,外环与E6经疏水作用相接,内环相邻原聚体间形成三链β折叠(β-hairpin)。 (六)分类揭示转录条件下存在去盖孔道状态。de novo(从头)分类仅在转录条件下一致发现缺乏外环(E8)与基环(L3)的第3类结构,即“去盖孔道(uncapped pore)”;共检测到1,397个此类颗粒,约占该条件孔道总数的一半,且其在完整与破裂核心间无显著定位偏好。 (七)中央杆状密度位置可变。杆状密度(高约9 nm)与孔道轴强对齐,主要绕轴旋转而非倾斜,轴向位置呈连续变异性(标准差约1.3–1.5 nm),表明位置缩短源于位置异质性;AF3系统筛选显示病毒RNA解旋酶I8(以单体形式发挥功能)被一致定位于管腔中央,其预测形状、尺寸及与L3的交联(I8残基378与L3残基272,C α -C α 距离约16 ?,在DSSO约35 ?跨度约束内)均与杆状密度相符,提示I8为合理候选。 (八)细胞内原位孔道架构与体外结构一致。以MOI 100感染HeLa细胞30分钟后行原位cryo-ET与STA,获得159个颗粒,约40 ?分辨率的重建再现了六个周围A10三聚体及外环、内环、基环与中央杆等关键架构特征,支持该结构在感染细胞内的生物学相关性。 **讨论与结论** 讨论部分将结构置于功能背景:孔道全部四种组分(E8、E6、L3与I8)均与痘病毒早期转录相关——E8为转录能力所需,E6参与成熟病毒组装且体外转录必需,L3缺陷病毒仅产生痕量早期mRNA,I8缺陷病毒无感染性。该孔道形成连续亲水通道,其负电表面与选择性mRNA转位孔相似,概念上可类比核孔复合体(nuclear pore complex, NPC)与冠状病毒感染诱导的膜孔。三层架构可能赋予各环不同功能:L3环作为mRNA进入中央通道的门户并穿透核心壁,E6层作为由六个A10三聚体固定的支架,E8层提供面向细胞质的mRNA出口;转录条件下观察到的E8/L3去盖现象可能反映孔道功能状态转变。杆状密度在两种条件下持续存在,其动力学特征与AF3预测的I8形状一致,结合I8的mRNA释放需求,研究人员提出I8为杆状密度候选的假说:mRNA输出可能由解旋酶主动驱动而非自由扩散,通道与杆间约2 nm间隙几何上兼容单链RNA通过。Calcraft等的同期独立研究解析了相同三组分(E8、E6、L3)的六聚体排列,与本研究相互印证,但其基于已有图谱的分类策略未观察到NTP添加后的去盖状态,本研究的de novo分类策略检测到更广泛的构象状态。综上,孔道复合物的架构、蛋白组成、电学性质与动态行为共同支持其参与(直接或间接)早期mRNA自核心释放的假说,但精确机制作用、杆状结构功能及感染早期E8/L3解离的调控等问题仍有待未来原位结构功能研究阐明。 **研究背景**痘病毒(poxvirus)是在宿主细胞质内复制的双链DNA病毒,涵盖天花病毒(Variola virus)与引发Mpox(猴痘)国际关注的突发公共卫生事件的Mpox病毒。其成熟病毒粒子(mature virion, MV)呈砖形,包裹双凹核心(core)及侧体(lateral bodies)。病毒进入细胞后,核心被释放至细胞质,其内转录机器可立即启动一百余种早期信使RNA(messenger RNA, mRNA)的合成,转录本随后释放入细胞质供翻译。然而,这些mRNA如何跨越核心壁(core wall)离开核心,数十年来悬而未决。早期研究虽在核心表面栅栏层(palisade layer)中观察到由A10三聚体环绕的孔状结构并推测其为mRNA释放位点,但分辨率限制使其蛋白组成无法确证,构成理解痘病毒早期基因表达的关键空白。**研究开展、主要结论与意义**针对这一空白,研究人员以牛痘病毒(vaccinia virus, VACV)为对象,整合冷冻电子断层扫描(cryo-electron tomography, cryo-ET)、亚断层图平均(subtomogram averaging, STA)、交联质谱(cross-linking mass spectrometry, XL-MS)与AlphaFold3(AF3)建模,首次解析痘病毒核心内多聚体孔道复合物的分子架构(分辨率约8.2 ?)。研究确定孔道由E8、E6与L3组装成跨越核心壁与栅栏层的三层空心管道,并提示管腔中央杆状密度可能对应病毒RNA解旋酶(I8),为“痘病毒核心mRNA释放孔”假说提供了首个结构性实证。该工作发表于《Nature Communications》,深化了对痘病毒早期基因表达结构基础的认识。**主要技术方法**研究人员将纯化的VACV Western nm),含外环、内环、基环及中央杆状密度,C对称性经随机化检验确认源自数据本身。(四)XL-MS鉴定孔道复合物组分。XL-MS在两个生物学重复中鉴定出233个蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用(protein-protein interactions, records.content: 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 HIV感染者遇上猴痘:风险会增加吗?该如何应对? 2026-10-29 13:23 来源: 大东北生活资讯 发布于:北京市 目前,猴痘疫情已在全球140多个国家和地区持续流行。截至2026年5月,全球累计报告超过18.7万例猴痘确诊病例。一个现象值得注意:全球约40%的猴痘病例同时感染人类免疫缺陷病毒(HIV),我国部分地区报告比例也高达35%~50%。对于本身已经感染 HIV的人群而言,猴痘的威胁与普通人群并不完全相同,需要给予特别关注。 一、为什么HIV感染者猴痘感染比例高? (一)由于部分HIV感染者仍持续存在多性伴、无保护性行为等高风险行为,在密切接触的过程中,皮肤黏膜直接接触到猴痘患者皮疹渗出液、病变分泌物的概率升高,增加了猴痘病毒的暴露与感染机会。 (二)与免疫功能正常的普通人群相比,CD4细胞水平偏低、病毒未控制的HIV感染者在接触猴痘病毒后,机体抵御病毒入侵的能力更弱,控制病毒扩散的能力受限,感染猴痘发生重症或病程延长的风险更高。 对于已经感染HIV的人来说,如果感染了猴痘,免疫功能的状态会直接影响猴痘的病情轻重、病程长短和最终预后。 二、HIV感染者感染猴痘后,可能面临哪些后果? (一)症状更重。在未经规范艾滋病抗病毒药物治疗(ART)或未得到有效控制的HIV感染者中,感染猴痘后更容易出现肛门疼痛、尿急、直肠出血、脓性或血性便以及直肠炎,严重时还可能累及肺、眼和中枢神经系统。 (二)病程更长。普通人群感染猴痘后,多数可在2~4周内自行痊愈。而免疫功能较差的HIV感染者,往往会出现皮疹愈合缓慢、病毒排出时间延长、住院时间增加的情况,不仅恢复时间更长,具备传播性的时间也会延长 。 (三)更容易发生继发感染和并发症。HIV本身会造成免疫功能下降,在此基础上再感染猴痘,会进一步加重机体的免疫负担,增加继发细菌、真菌等机会性感染的风险,使病情更为复杂,并发症发生概率也更高。 (四)诊疗管理更加复杂。感染者需要同时兼顾HIV抗病毒治疗和猴痘对症治疗,医生需要密切关注两种治疗药物之间的相互作用,监测免疫功能恢复情况,及时发现和处理并发症,整体诊疗方案比单一疾病更为复杂。 研究表明,免疫功能状态是影响疾病预后的关键因素,接受规范ART且HIV得到有效抑制的HIV感染者,感染猴痘后的临床表现和康复时间与未感染HIV的人群相近。而未接受规范ART、未得到控制、CD4细胞计数较低(尤其低于200个/μL),以及合并其他基础疾病的HIV感染者,发生持续性、播散性或重症猴痘以及住院和死亡的风险更高,需格外关注。 三、HIV感染者该如何应对猴痘风险? (一)做好个人防护。避免与不明原因皮疹者发生密切接触或性接触;不共用毛巾、寝具等生活用品;前往疫情流行地区时,应避免接触患病人员及可能携带病毒的野生动物,降低猴痘感染风险。 (二)尽早发现、及时就诊。出现发热、皮疹、淋巴结肿大等症状,尤其有相关接触史或旅行史者,一定要及时前往正规医院的感染科或皮肤科就诊,并主动告知相关流行病学史。 展开全文 (三)坚持规范治疗。遵医嘱坚持服用HIV抗病毒药物,避免自行停药或中断治疗。持续抑制病毒复制、促进CD4细胞恢复,有助于降低猴痘重症及不良结局风险。 综上,对于HIV感染者而言,提高对猴痘的警惕、做好个人防护、出现症状早就医,同时坚持规范抗病毒治疗、维持良好的免疫状态,能够最大程度降低猴痘带来的健康风险,减少重症和不良结局的发生。 (中国疾控艾防中心 郭尔欣 秦倩倩) 参考文献: World Health Organization.
